title: Gaussian quantile divergence at zero
statement: Let $\Phi(t)$ be the cumulative distribution function of the standard Gaussian probability measure on $\mathbb R$, and define $Q(\alpha)=\inf\{t\in\mathbb R:\alpha\leq\Phi(t)\}$ for every real $\alpha$. As $\alpha$ tends to $0$ through positive values, $Q(\alpha)$ tends to $-\infty$.
replaced:
Let $\Phi(t)=\int_{-\infty}^{t}e^{-x^2/2}/\sqrt{2\pi}\,dx$, and let $Q(\alpha)=\inf\{t\in\mathbb R:\alpha\le\Phi(t)\}$ for $0<\alpha<1$ and $Q(\alpha)=0$ otherwise. As a real $\alpha$ tends to zero through positive values, the quantile tends to negative infinity:
\[
\lim_{\alpha\to0^+}Q(\alpha)=-\infty.
\]
